audit.report: A replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile, pid 17687) sat idle in transaction for 4 seconds, holding locks that blocked checkout sessions and dropped success to 60% against a 95% SLO, putting $7,329/min of revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker; the Continuity Guardian accepted after confirming the workload is BATCH_REPLAYABLE with a 4-minute replay cost, no active change-calendar window, and no protected settlements in flight. Authority authorized the termination, the executor killed the session, and verification showed checkout recovered to 100% success (36/36) with no lock waits and all protected operations intact. Total negotiation and recovery took 47.5 seconds in a single round.
audit.root_cause: The inventory_reconcile batch job (batch_replayable_inventory) opened a transaction and went idle, holding locks that blocked checkout sessions and degraded the checkout SLO.
lessons: Add an idle-in-transaction timeout (e.g., 30s) for batch_replayable_inventory so the database auto-terminates stalled workers before they block checkout.
Instrument inventory_reconcile to emit a heartbeat or progress metric; alert if a checkpoint isn't advanced within its typical 900s runtime so on-call can intervene before locks accumulate.
Document and test the 4-minute replay procedure for inventory_reconcile in the runbook so the team can confidently re-run it after an emergency termination.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian gathered all required evidence (lock holder, workload registry, change calendar, protected settlements, business impact) in the first proposal, and the Continuity Guardian accepted without objection, so no rounds were wasted and no invariants were overridden.
follow_ups: Configure idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for the batch_worker role to prevent recurrence.
Add a Prometheus alert on inventory_reconcile checkpoint lag > 15 minutes.
Run a fire-drill replay of inventory_reconcile to validate the 4-minute recovery claim.
